one_liner: Embeddable non-blocking Java HTTP server (Red Hat); a 2014 build topped Kore, libmicrohttpd and a 4-worker nginx in a 2015 hello-world test.
what_it_does: Undertow is a Java web server on XNIO non-blocking I/O, shipped as Maven modules: undertow-core (HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, AJP and the HttpHandler chain), undertow-servlet (Servlet 4.0/5.0/6.0 per the README) and a Jakarta WebSocket implementation. You embed it with Undertow.builder().addHttpListener(...).setHandler(...).build().start() and write handlers against HttpServerExchange. It replaces nothing in nginx's configuration: it is an application server you program, not a reverse proxy or static-file front end.
how_it_is_fast: Handlers run directly on XNIO I/O threads (one per logical CPU by default: Math.max(availableProcessors, 2)), so a non-blocking response like the benchmark's needs no thread hand-off. Blocking work goes to a worker pool of 8 threads per I/O thread through exchange.dispatch(). Buffers come from a pooled allocator that picks direct 16 KB-minus-20-byte buffers when the heap limit is at least 128 MB. The Date header string is cached and invalidated by a timer once a second (DateUtils). The measured 1.0.0.Final release parsed requests with a build-time generated state machine (HttpRequestParser$$generated) that has a fast path for 'GET ' and returns interned strings for common methods, protocols and headers; current main replaces it with a hand-written RequestParser.
when_to_use: JVM services that want an embedded HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 server with a small, explicit handler-chain API rather than a full framework
Request handlers that can answer without blocking, so they run on the I/O thread with no hand-off; this is the case the benchmark measured
Applications that need an embeddable Servlet 6.0 or Jakarta WebSocket container in the same process as non-blocking handlers
Long-running services where JVM start-up, JIT warm-up and a resident heap are acceptable and steady-state keep-alive throughput matters
when_not_to_use: As a replacement for nginx's proxying, TLS termination or static-file serving by configuration; with Undertow you write and run Java code

Spring Boot 4.x applications: the Spring Boot 4.0 migration guide drops Undertow support ('Spring Boot 4 requires a Servlet 6.1 baseline, with which Undertow is not yet compatible'); use Tomcat or Jetty there
Tail-latency-sensitive services chosen on this evidence: in the same table libmicrohttpd's p99 was 1.28 ms against Undertow's 3.29 ms (Undertow's four runs ranged 2.16 to 4.08 ms)
Short-lived processes or tight memory budgets, where JVM start-up, warm-up and heap size dominate; none of that is in the throughput figure
If you need current numbers against C/C++ servers: Undertow has no entry in the HttpArena suite (frameworks/undertow returns 404) and its own repo has only JMH microbenchmarks

integration.dependencies: XNIO (xnio-api, xnio-nio 3.8.16.Final), jboss-logging, jboss-threads; the servlet and WebSocket modules add the Jakarta Servlet and WebSocket APIs
integration.min_toolchain: Java 17 for 2.4.x (2.4.4.Final, 2026-10-02) and main (2.5.0.Alpha1-SNAPSHOT); Java 11 for 2.3.x (2.3.26.Final); Maven to build from source
integration.platforms: any platform with a supported JVM (pure Java on JDK NIO through XNIO; no native transport)
integration.thread_safety: Each exchange starts on an XNIO I/O thread; blocking calls there stall every connection on that thread, so handlers check isInIoThread() and dispatch blocking work to the worker pool (exchange.dispatch, startBlocking for stream I/O). The no-argument dispatch() is deprecated as 'hard to use safely'.

gotchas: Old artifact measured: benchmarks/undertow/build.gradle asks for 'io.undertow:undertow-core:1.0.0+'. Gradle treats a trailing '+' as a prefix match (SubVersionSelector: candidate.startsWith("1.0.0"), in Gradle 2.9 of late 2015 and in current master), so the candidates are the 61 versions starting with '1.0.0' on Maven Central (Alpha1-22, Beta1-33, CR1-5, Final), and, because Gradle's version comparator ranks 'final' above any other qualifier, the build resolves 1.0.0.Final (tagged 2014-02-10), which excludes even 1.0.1.Final to 1.0.19.Final and every later 1.x release, so the 2015 run measured a jar from February 2014. Current releases are 2.4.4.Final and 2.3.26.Final. The JVM version and flags are not stated, and build.gradle sets no JVM arguments.

Response sizes derived from page data (MB/s over req/s): Undertow sends exactly 137 bytes, the same as libmicrohttpd (status line, Connection, Content-Type, Content-Length 11, a Date header and 'Hello World'). That makes the 1.16x over libmicrohttpd (12-thread epoll pool) the like-for-like row. Kore sends 191 bytes and Onion 197, so they do more work per request. The nginx echo row sends 119 bytes with Date and Server stripped, but runs only worker_processes 4 against Undertow's 12 default I/O threads on the 6-core/12-thread Xeon, so the 1.62x over nginx comes from configuration.

README rows are the best of four 20 s runs for every server, and the ratios hold on four-run means: Undertow 612,590 req/s against libmicrohttpd 531,964 (1.15x), Kore 570,784 (1.07x) and nginx echo 376,520 (1.63x), all derived from page data. The p99 column is unstable for some servers: Kore's run 01 p99 was 87.03 ms and Onion's 105.21 ms, while the README shows 3.99 ms and 2.82 ms from their best runs.

SECURITY.md lists only 2.2.x and 2.3.x as supported, although 2.4.x has been released since May 2026. WebSearch snippets list recent CVEs: CVE-2025-9784 (HTTP/2 'MadeYouReset' stream-reset DoS), CVE-2026-3260 (multipart/form-data on GET written to disk; fix reported in 2.4.0.Beta1) and CVE-2026-5680 (WebSocket permessage-deflate memory exhaustion; fixed in 2.4.3.Final per Mend). The GitHub Security tab has no advisories because disclosure goes through Red Hat SecAlert, so track Red Hat errata.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Undertow over Netty (same 2015 table, 422,580 req/s) when you want a ready HTTP and Servlet server with a handler API instead of building the pipeline yourself. For current evidence against nginx 1.31.4, the siblings Vert.x, Quarkus and Helidon SE have recent HttpArena rows, and Undertow does not.
verified_claims_summary: nanoant/WebFrameworkBenchmark (December 2015, Xeon E5-1650 v2, Ubuntu 14.04, Linux 3.16; wrk with 12 threads and 100 keep-alive connections on the same host; 20 s runs after a 10 s warm-up; best of four) measured a hello-world handler on Undertow 1.0.0.Final with an unstated JVM at 616,547 req/s. That is 1.08x Kore (make NOTLS=1, 12 workers), 1.16x libmicrohttpd (cc -O3, 12-thread epoll pool, identical 137-byte responses), 1.27x Onion, 1.62x OpenResty nginx with the echo module at 4 workers, and 2.40x Crow (c++ -O3). All ratios are derived from page data, and Undertow's p99 is worse than libmicrohttpd's and Onion's.
status_note: Actively maintained by Red Hat (Apache-2.0, 3.8k stars, last commit 2026-10-08, 2.4.4.Final on 2026-10-02) and copyable as a Maven dependency. The only evidence is a 2015 single-author benchmark of the 2014 1.0.0.Final jar, so treat the ratios as historical.
